# Offline original MSI qualification

The **Windows Offline Original MSI Proof** workflow uses a disposable Windows 2022 runner and an existing successful installer build. It never rebuilds a package. The draft pull request pins the original 1.6.0 installer from workflow run `44768324452`, source `83b0a98b278b98e779842538f811b2c6f5b6b4c8`. After this workflow is available for manual dispatch, supply the original Windows build run ID, full source SHA, expected app version, and expected database revision for another candidate. The original run must have its installer artifacts available.

Setup downloads and hashes each original artifact ZIP, matches MSI and all CAB bytes and Media entries to verified build provenance, and stages the pinned Playwright dependency lock before the measured interval. A preview execution of the independently scheduled SYSTEM recovery task must succeed before the harness disconnects the network. The watchdog automatically restores the original adapters after four minutes if the controller stops. Setup, installation, and network controls are guarded for the dedicated GitHub-hosted workflow.

The proof disables the live non-loopback adapters and repeatedly observes no operational external links. It resolves `api.github.com` once online and checks direct TCP connectivity to the same addresses before, during, and after isolation. The test uses the original MSI with `/i`, verifies the installed product registration, and launches the installed shell and packaged loopback sidecar as a fresh Windows user at medium integrity. The tracked first-use WebView2 journey imports/reviews source pixels, reopens them in the editor, and downloads YOLO. A second installed desktop and sidecar launch reopen the same managed profile and verify the exact saved image hash and annotation. The interval is invalid if the watchdog deadline is reached or the independent adapter log has an unobserved gap. Reconnection, temporary account removal, and uninstall finish before uploading evidence.

Download `ReefVision-Windows-Offline-MSI-Proof`. `offline-install-report.json` records PASS, the original MSI, installed binary hashes, source/test identity, control phases, launch IDs, and persisted review. `offline-links.jsonl`, `watchdog.jsonl`, `verified-transport.json`, `verified-payload.json`, installer logs, and the native test's own receipt document their inputs and outcomes. The hosted runner already includes WebView2 and Windows components. Installation on a disconnected Windows system that lacks these prerequisites is outside this proof.
